subject: Token delivery gap — reconciliation and action lane
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Lily Zhang <lily@finovate.io>, Rajesh Patel <r.patel@clearpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Token delivery gap — reconciliation and action lane

Hi Lily / Rajesh,

Thank you again for the patience while we finished the internal analysis. I’m writing with a concise reconciliation of what happened during yesterday’s token-delivery gaps and the concrete actions we’re committing to. We know this impacted Finovate’s production routing and I want to make next steps explicit.

Summary (short):
- Impact: 09:05–09:42 PDT on 2027-07-27 — 3% of requests for your tokenized sessions saw delayed completions (timeouts or extra retries).
- Immediate mitigation: we rolled a targeted config rollback at 09:44 PDT which restored normal delivery rates.
- Root cause (high level): autoscaler interaction with the KV cache eviction path under a burst of short-lived sessions caused transient memory pressure and premature eviction of live session state, resulting in token resend attempts.

What we’re sharing here: a short timeline, an RCA summary, and an owner-assigned action lane with deadlines. I’ve attached a short extract of logs and a CSV of cache metrics for your team to validate.

Timeline (key events):
- 09:02 PDT — burst of short sessions from Finovate load generator (avg length 12 tokens).
- 09:05 PDT — memory pressure observed on two GPU workers serving your region (KV cache eviction rate spikes).
- 09:07 PDT — first customer report (inbound support ticket).
- 09:18 PDT — autoscaler triggered scale-up; new nodes came up but cache warmup lagged.
- 09:30 PDT — elevated retry rate observed; we began mitigations.
- 09:44 PDT — config rollback (temporary lowering of eviction aggressiveness) pushed; delivery rates normalized by 09:46 PDT.

High-level RCA (concise):
- Trigger: an unusual mix of many short-lived sessions and a scheduled autoscaler policy change that coincided with model shard rebalancing. The rebalancing path cleared some shared cache pointers earlier than intended.
- Mechanism: when the autoscaler removed and added shards, a race condition in the cache eviction code allowed active KV entries to be marked as evictable before the new worker had the chance to fully rehydrate the session state. This produced transient misses and prompted token resend logic in the application layer.
- Why it wasn’t caught earlier: this path only surfaces with the specific combination of (1) short session workload distribution, (2) autoscaler churn within a 30s window, and (3) a recent cache optimization we shipped last month. It’s low frequency but real under heavy short-session traffic.

Immediate actions we took (already done):
- Rolled back the eviction aggressiveness flag (09:44 PDT).
- Increased autoscaler minimum stability window to avoid rapid churn sequences (09:50 PDT).
- Throttled non-critical background rebalances for your tenant for 48h.

Planned remediation (owner / ETA):
- M1: Patch race in cache eviction -> engineering fix and test (owner: Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2027-08-04.
- M2: Add a tenant-aware warmup handshake during shard addition to prevent live-state evictions (owner: Marissa Cole) — ETA: 2027-08-11.
- M3: Expanded integration test with synthetic short-session workload to add regression guard (owner: Jonas Weber) — ETA: 2027-08-06.
- M4: Compensation/credits review and customer-specific verification plan (owner: Vivek Kulkarni) — ETA: 2027-07-30.

Attachments included: incident_log_excerpt.txt (log snippets), kvcache-metrics.csv (eviction/warmup counters), timeline-slide-deck.pdf (2 slides).

Request: can you confirm whether the attached log snippets map to the sessions you saw fail? Also let me know if you’d like a short technical walkthrough this week — I can arrange a 30-minute call with engineering.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take these seriously and will update you as we close the remediation lane.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Global Head, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Jul 28, 2027 at 9:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Token delivery gap — reconciliation and action lane

Lily — thanks for the rapid read and the call invite. I’m Jonas (lead on inference runtime). I’ll host an engineering walkthrough of the fix approach and tests. Below is a slightly deeper technical note to help Finovate prepare questions.

Deeper technical note (engineer -> engineer):
- Root cause detail: the eviction path used a soft-ttl + owner-pointer check. During shard removal we were clearing owner-pointers before the receiving shard completed the rehydration handshake. That gap is the race window.
- Why retries happened: our frontend token orchestration treats a cache miss as a non-fatal event and attempts a retry/resend. With multiple clients on short sessions that retry window amplified the visible failures.

Planned short-term validation:
- I’ll push a canary patch to CI that introduces an atomic handshake (handover token) for shard moves — this prevents marking entries as evictable until confirmed. Canary ETA: 2027-08-02.
- We’ll add a targeted perf/regression job that simulates 10k short sessions with 20% churn; results will be shared.

Action items (updated):
- Jonas: canary handshake patch + CI run — ETA 2027-08-02.
- Jonas: regression job + results to Finovate — ETA 2027-08-04.
- Marissa: tenant warmup handshake design doc + schedule — ETA 2027-08-11.
- Vivek: credits proposal draft and verification plan — ETA 2027-07-30.

I’ll prepare a 20–25 minute walkthrough focused on the handshake and regression design. Vivek — can you confirm Thursday 11:00 PDT for the call?

—Jonas
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Lily — thanks for taking the call today and for the candid feedback. Recap and next steps below to keep a single source of truth as we move toward closure.

Recap of the call (7/30):
- Walkthrough covered the handshake patch approach (Jonas) and tenant warmup plan (Marissa).
- Finovate asked for a verification replay and a proportional credits proposal.

Committed next steps and owners: 
- Credits proposal: Vivek to send draft credit amount and calculation methodology by EOD 2027-07-30 (in flight).
- Canary rollout: Jonas to run the handshake canary in a controlled environment and share results (ETA: 2027-08-02).
- Regression test results: Jonas to deliver simulated run and metrics for Finovate (ETA: 2027-08-04).
- Warmup handshake design doc: Marissa to deliver and schedule implementation window (ETA: 2027-08-11).
- Verification plan: joint runbook for Finovate validation including start/end times, probe IDs, and expected signal thresholds (owner: Vivek) — ETA: 2027-07-31.

Next meeting: provisional check-in Friday 2027-08-06 10:00 PDT pending canary results. I’ll share a calendar invite after Jonas posts initial CI artifacts.

If anything here looks off, flag it and I’ll correct. We’ll keep you updated as each milestone lands.

Best regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Global Head, Customer Reliability
